u02-rem-mid.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'They bought the Lord, betrayed for silver' renders ὡς τὸν κύριον ἀργυρίου προδοθέντα … ἐξωνήσαντο (ἐξωνέομαι, 'buy'). This was corrected from the Greek in this re-read, and the Greek has the buyers as subject. Isaiah 63:19, Genesis 3:19 and Romans 7:14 correctly identify the quoted texts; 'Ps 43,13a' is the edition's fragment heading. 'That they did not turn aside … nor did they swerve' renders the articular infinitives (τὸ μὴ μεταβάλλεσθαι … μηδ' … ἀποκλῖναι) stating what they actually did, not commands. 'They do not entirely abandon the very not-going to idols' is οὐ παντελῶς ἀπολείπουσιν: they still keep away from idols, which is what the English says. The Greek has ὑπ' αὐτῶν ('by them'). The rest are style.

u02-rem-mid.resolution: I found no meaning error. In ὁδοῦ τῆς ἐπιταχθείσης the commanded thing is the road of piety; 'the path of piety … that had been commanded them' says exactly that. 'Worship of idols' makes explicit the context of the three youths (Dan 3). 'This is not present as something pious' renders οὐκ εὐσεβῆ πρόσεστι. 'Which are brought up by them' renders ἀναγόμενα ὑπ' αὐτῶν.
